questions.prompt: Describe two shots from a net/wall game of your choice, giving key technique points and the tactical purpose of each.
questions.model: Activity: badminton. Clear: a high, deep shot to the back of the court. The player hits it high and deep so the shuttle comes down behind the opponent. Tactical purpose: it gains time, so the player can recover to the base position, and it pushes the opponent to the back of the court. Drop shot: disguised as a clear, so the preparation looks the same until contact, and the shuttle lands just over the net. Tactical purpose: it draws the opponent forward to the net, leaving the space behind them open for a later shot.

questions.prompt: Describe the forearm pass (dig) in volleyball.
questions.model: The dig, or forearm pass, is played with the forearms together to form a platform, with the legs bent. The player moves under the ball early so that it meets the forearms, and the contact is made on the forearms so the ball rebounds upwards. Power comes from the legs: the player pushes up with the legs to send the ball towards the target, not by swinging the arms. The pass keeps the ball in play so a team-mate can set it for a spike.
